dedupe_keys.name: operandum emilia romagna coastal nature based solutions modelling seagrass and artificial dune bellocchio beach

description: These two datasets hold model results for nature-based solutions against coastal erosion and marine flooding at Bellocchio beach, Lido di Spina, on the northern Adriatic coast of Emilia-Romagna, Italy. One tests an artificial dune built with natural materials and a nearshore seagrass belt, giving morphological evolution, sedimentation and erosion, and maximum flood depth results. The other gives WAVEWATCH III wave time series for the present (2010 to 2019) and future (2040 to 2049, RCP8.5 with Med-CORDEX winds) climate, with and without a Zostera marina seagrass meadow represented by a modified bottom dissipation term. They were produced by Arpae, the University of Bologna and CMCC in the H2020 OPERANDUM open-air laboratories project and published on Zenodo in 2021 and 2022 under CC BY 4.0, as downloadable zipped model outputs, Excel time series and PDF guides (about 28 and 93 MB). Caveats: results are for one beach and one set of designs, are model outputs, not observations, and file formats inside the archives are described only in the PDFs. It supports calibration and scenario testing of coastal green infrastructure against storm surge and erosion; a related record is the Oppla nature-based solutions repository.
